citations.quote: A **finite fusion transfer count model** consists of a finite nonempty label set $I$, a distinguished label $0\in I$, and an explicitly supplied matrix $N=(N_{ab})_{a,b\in I}$ whose entries lie in $\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. The entry $N_{ab}$ is the multiplicity of elementary transitions from label $b$ to label $a$; formally, the transition copies from $b$ to $a$ are the triples $(b,a,j)$ with integer $1\leq j\leq N_{ab}$. A length-$n$ path is a sequence of $n+1$ labels together with a chosen transition copy between each consecutive pair. View each natural-number entry as a real number under the usual inclusion $\mathbb N\subset\mathbb R$. For a finite set $J$ and $F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, $F^J$ means the functions $J\to F$, with pointwise addition $(x+y)_j=x_j+y_j$ and scalar multiplication $(\lambda x)_j=\lambda x_j$. For real matrices $A,B$ indexed by $I$, define $(A+B)_{ab}:=A_{ab}+B_{ab}$. Their action on $x\in\mathbb R^I$ is $(Ax)_a:=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}x_b$. Matrix multiplication is $(AB)_{ac}:=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}B_{bc}$; it is associative by regrouping finite sums. These definitions are compatible because $((AB)x)_a=\sum_{b,c\in I}A_{ab}B_{bc}x_c=\sum_{b\in I}A_{ab}(Bx)_b=(A(Bx))_a$, and $((A+B)C)_{ac}=\sum_b(A_{ab}+B_{ab})C_{bc}=(AC)_{ac}+(BC)_{ac}$. Thus the natural-entry powers can also act on real vectors and the addition used below distributes over matrix multiplication. Let $I_I$ be the identity matrix with entries $(I_I)_{ab}=1$ if $a=b$ and $0$ otherwise, and use the power convention $N^0:=I_I$ and $N^{n+1}:=NN^n$ for $n\geq0$. Define the vacuum-return count $D_n:=(N^n)_{00}$. If $D_n>0$, set $H_n:=\mathbb C^{D_n}$, with coordinates $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{D_n})$ and inner product $\langle x,y\rangle:=\sum_{j=1}^{D_n}x_j\overline{y_j}$, linear in the first argument. This pairing satisfies the inner-product axioms of [[def-inner-product-space]]: finite distributivity gives $\langle\alpha x+\beta z,y\rangle=\alpha\langle x,y\rangle+\beta\langle z,y\rangle$, and conjugating the finite sum gives $\overline{\langle y,x\rangle}=\sum_j\overline{y_j}x_j=\langle x,y\rangle$. Writing $x_j=a_j+ib_j$ with real $a_j,b_j$ gives $\langle x,x\rangle=\sum_j(a_j^2+b_j^2)\geq0$; if this sum is zero, each nonnegative summand is zero, hence every $a_j=b_j=0$ and $x=0$. Conversely $x=0$ gives zero. The conjugation identities used here follow directly from $\overline{a+ib}=a-ib$ and finite distributivity. Therefore $H_n$ is a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; its coordinate unit vectors form a basis since every $x$ equals their linear combination with coefficients $x_j$, and a zero combination forces every coefficient to vanish. Let $I_{H_n}$ be its identity endomorphism and define $\rho_n:=D_n^{-1}I_{H_n}$. If $D_n=0$, no normalized operator $\rho_n$ is assigned. The matrix $N$ is model data; no fusion category, quantum group, or representation is presumed to realize it.

Let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set. For each $\alpha\in I$, let $H_\alpha$ and $K_\alpha$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and give

$$H_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}(H_\alpha\otimes K_\alpha)$$

the orthogonal direct-sum inner product: distinct summands are orthogonal and the inner product within a summand is the Hilbert tensor-product inner product. On elementary tensors that inner product is $\langle x\otimes y,x'\otimes y'\rangle=\langle x,x'\rangle\langle y,y'\rangle$. A map $T\otimes U$ acts by $(T\otimes U)(x\otimes y)=Tx\otimes Uy$, and a direct-sum map acts blockwise with zero off-diagonal blocks.

A complex-linear endomorphism is a linear map from a vector space to itself. A density matrix on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space is a self-adjoint endomorphism with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one; it is faithful when all eigenvalues are strictly positive. These are the conventions used for the finite density matrices in the earlier modular-balance result. The summand indexed by $\alpha$ is called the $\alpha$ sector. For each $\alpha$, fix a faithful density matrix $\chi_\alpha$ on $K_\alpha$. Let $\mathbf p=(p_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ satisfy $p_\alpha>0$ and $\sum_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha=1$, and let $\rho_\alpha$ be density matrices on $H_\alpha$. Define the encoded endomorphism

$$\mathcal E_\chi(\mathbf p,\rho):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\,\rho_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha.$$

When this encoded endomorphism is a density matrix, call it the encoded reduced state. The logical data are $\mathbf p$ and $\{\rho_\alpha\}$; the ancillary matrices $\{\chi_\alpha\}$ are held fixed. For a second strictly positive probability vector $\mathbf q$ and faithful density matrices $\sigma_\alpha$ on the same $H_\alpha$, write $\sigma_A:=\mathcal E_\chi(\mathbf q,\sigma)$ for the encoded reference endomorphism.

This is a finite-dimensional algebraic model. The definition makes no gravitational interpretation and does not identify a matrix entropy term with a geometric area.

Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set. For each $\alpha\in I$, let $H_\alpha,K_\alpha$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. A density matrix is a self-adjoint endomorphism with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one; it is faithful when all its eigenvalues are strictly positive. Let $p_\alpha,q_\alpha>0$ with $\sum_\alpha p_\alpha=\sum_\alpha q_\alpha=1$, let $\rho_\alpha$ be a density matrix on $H_\alpha$, let $\sigma_\alpha$ be a faithful density matrix on $H_\alpha$, and let $\chi_\alpha$ be a fixed faithful density matrix on $K_\alpha$. Form the finite orthogonal direct sums

$$\rho_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\rho_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha,\qquad \sigma_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}q_\alpha\sigma_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha.$$

For a density matrix $\tau$, set $s(\tau):=-\sum_{\lambda_j(\tau)>0}\lambda_j(\tau)\log\lambda_j(\tau)$, with $0\log0:=0$, so entropy is in nats. For density matrices $\tau,\omega$ with faithful reference $\omega$, set $D(\tau\|\omega):=\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\tau)-\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\omega)$ using spectral logarithms on positive eigenvalues. Also define $H(\mathbf p):=-\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\log p_\alpha$ and $D_{\rm cl}(\mathbf p\|\mathbf q):=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\log(p_\alpha/q_\alpha)$. Then $\rho_A$ and $\sigma_A$ are density matrices, $\sigma_A$ is faithful, and

$$s(\rho_A)=H(\mathbf p)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\bigl(s(\rho_\alpha)+s(\chi_\alpha)\bigr),$$

$$D(\rho_A\|\sigma_A)=D_{\rm cl}(\mathbf p\|\mathbf q)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha D(\rho_\alpha\|\sigma_\alpha).$$

These are exact finite-dimensional matrix identities; no literal black-hole area, universal Ryu–Takayanagi formula, continuum limit, or gravitational entropy claim follows.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

derivations.claim: For $n=0$, the unique path of length zero is the empty path from $0$ to $0$, and there is no length-zero path from $0$ to any $a\ne0$. Thus the number of length-zero paths from $0$ to $a$ is $(I_I)_{a0}=(N^0)_{a0}=(e_0)_a$.

If $D_n>0$, then $D_n$ is a positive integer and $\rho_n=D_n^{-1}I_{H_n}$ has eigenvalue $1/D_n$ with multiplicity $D_n$. Its trace is $D_n(1/D_n)=1$, and it is self-adjoint since $\langle\rho_n x,y\rangle=D_n^{-1}\langle x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho_n y\rangle$ with the real scalar $D_n^{-1}$, and its eigenvalues are nonnegative; hence it is a density matrix by [F2]. Substitution into [F3] gives $s(\rho_n)=-D_n(1/D_n)\log(1/D_n)=\log D_n$ by [F5].

Suppose for a fixed $n\geq0$ that the number of length-$n$ paths from $0$ to each $b\in I$ is $(N^n)_{b0}$. Every length-$(n+1)$ path from $0$ to $a$ has a unique penultimate label $b$ and a final transition copy from $b$ to $a$, so the number of such paths is $\sum_{b\in I}N_{ab}(N^n)_{b0}=(NN^n)_{a0}=(N^{n+1})_{a0}$ by the stated matrix-product and power conventions. Induction proves $(v_n)_a=(N^n)_{a0}$ for every $n\geq0$ and $a\in I$; in particular $v_0=e_0$ and $v_{n+1}=Nv_n$.

Under [A1], direct multiplication gives $N^2=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}=N+I_I$. Therefore $D_0=1$, $D_1=0$, and $D_2=1$. From the power recursion and associativity, $N^{n+2}=N^2N^n=(N+I_I)N^n=N^{n+1}+N^n$ for every $n\geq0$; taking the $(0,0)$ entry proves $D_{n+2}=D_{n+1}+D_n$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set. For each $\alpha\in I$, let $H_\alpha,K_\alpha$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. A density matrix is a self-adjoint endomorphism with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one; it is faithful when all its eigenvalues are strictly positive. Let $p_\alpha,q_\alpha>0$ with $\sum_\alpha p_\alpha=\sum_\alpha q_\alpha=1$, let $\rho_\alpha$ be a density matrix on $H_\alpha$, let $\sigma_\alpha$ be a faithful density matrix on $H_\alpha$, and let $\chi_\alpha$ be a fixed faithful density matrix on $K_\alpha$. Form the finite orthogonal direct sums

$$\rho_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\rho_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha,\qquad \sigma_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}q_\alpha\sigma_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha.$$

For a density matrix $\tau$, set $s(\tau):=-\sum_{\lambda_j(\tau)>0}\lambda_j(\tau)\log\lambda_j(\tau)$, with $0\log0:=0$, so entropy is in nats. For density matrices $\tau,\omega$ with faithful reference $\omega$, set $D(\tau\|\omega):=\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\tau)-\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\omega)$ using spectral logarithms on positive eigenvalues. Also define $H(\mathbf p):=-\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\log p_\alpha$ and $D_{\rm cl}(\mathbf p\|\mathbf q):=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\log(p_\alpha/q_\alpha)$. Then $\rho_A$ and $\sigma_A$ are density matrices, $\sigma_A$ is faithful, and

$$s(\rho_A)=H(\mathbf p)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\bigl(s(\rho_\alpha)+s(\chi_\alpha)\bigr),$$

$$D(\rho_A\|\sigma_A)=D_{\rm cl}(\mathbf p\|\mathbf q)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha D(\rho_\alpha\|\sigma_\alpha).$$

These are exact finite-dimensional matrix identities; no literal black-hole area, universal Ryu–Takayanagi formula, continuum limit, or gravitational entropy claim follows.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set. For each $\alpha\in I$, let $H_\alpha$ and $K_\alpha$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and give

$$H_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}(H_\alpha\otimes K_\alpha)$$

the orthogonal direct-sum inner product: distinct summands are orthogonal and the inner product within a summand is the Hilbert tensor-product inner product. On elementary tensors that inner product is $\langle x\otimes y,x'\otimes y'\rangle=\langle x,x'\rangle\langle y,y'\rangle$. A map $T\otimes U$ acts by $(T\otimes U)(x\otimes y)=Tx\otimes Uy$, and a direct-sum map acts blockwise with zero off-diagonal blocks.

A complex-linear endomorphism is a linear map from a vector space to itself. A density matrix on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space is a self-adjoint endomorphism with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one; it is faithful when all eigenvalues are strictly positive. These are the conventions used for the finite density matrices in the earlier modular-balance result. The summand indexed by $\alpha$ is called the $\alpha$ sector. For each $\alpha$, fix a faithful density matrix $\chi_\alpha$ on $K_\alpha$. Let $\mathbf p=(p_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ satisfy $p_\alpha>0$ and $\sum_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha=1$, and let $\rho_\alpha$ be density matrices on $H_\alpha$. Define the encoded endomorphism

$$\mathcal E_\chi(\mathbf p,\rho):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\,\rho_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha.$$

When this encoded endomorphism is a density matrix, call it the encoded reduced state. The logical data are $\mathbf p$ and $\{\rho_\alpha\}$; the ancillary matrices $\{\chi_\alpha\}$ are held fixed. For a second strictly positive probability vector $\mathbf q$ and faithful density matrices $\sigma_\alpha$ on the same $H_\alpha$, write $\sigma_A:=\mathcal E_\chi(\mathbf q,\sigma)$ for the encoded reference endomorphism.

This is a finite-dimensional algebraic model. The definition makes no gravitational interpretation and does not identify a matrix entropy term with a geometric area.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.
